is_anopheles.evidence: The study uses laboratory-reared Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles funestus s.s. (Page 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions KDR and metabolic resistance in laboratory strains but does not report genotyping of any specific target markers (Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype counts, allele counts, or frequencies are provided for any population.

african_field_population.evidence: The study exclusively uses laboratory-reared mosquito strains (Ifakara, Kisumu, FUMOZ) rather than field-collected populations (Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study evaluating HLC methodology (Page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted at the Ifakara Health Institute, Bagamoyo-Kingani, Tanzania (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The paper was received in 2022 and published in 2023, indicating a recent study period (Page 13).

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a primary methodological study using established laboratory strains.

supplement.evidence: The study design does not include field genotyping, so no such data is expected in supplements.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the human landing catch (HLC) method as a proxy for protective efficacy of spatial repellents (transfluthrin) using laboratory-reared Anopheles and Aedes mosquitoes in a semi-field system in Tanzania. It does not report any genotyping of insecticide resistance markers in field populations.
